topic: Ttareungyi (따릉이), Seoul public bike: 2010 pilot 440 bikes, official Oct 2015; ~45,000 bikes at ~2,800 stations; app with English version; non-member day pass 1h ₩1,000 / 2h ₩2,000 / 3h ₩3,000 (3h added 2025-11-13); 365-day 1h pass ₩30,000; fees frozen 10 years; weekday rush hours 18% (07-09) + 26.3% (17-19); 100 mileage for rush-hour rebalancing; 113,000 rides 2015 to 43.85M in 2024; 5.06M members, 250.17M cumulative rides (Sep 2025); losses ₩10.9B 2023, ₩12.7B 2024. 2026 data leak deliberately left out.
title: In Seoul, a Bike Costs ₩1,000 an Hour

slides.headline: In Seoul, a bike costs **₩1,000 an hour.**
slides.note: Green wheels on almost every corner.

slides.headline: It's called **Ttareungyi**
slides.body: The name comes from "ttareung," the ring of a bike bell. Seoul tested it with 440 bikes in 2010 and launched it citywide in 2015.

slides.headline: About **45,000 bikes**
slides.body: They wait at around 2,800 stations across Seoul. Outside a subway exit, there's usually one nearby.

slides.headline: Unlock with **your phone**
slides.body: Pay in the app, scan the bike, ride. Return it at any station, not the one you started from. The app has an English version.

slides.headline: A year for **₩30,000**
slides.body: Members can buy a 365-day pass for 1-hour rides at ₩30,000, about $20. The prices haven't gone up in 10 years.

slides.headline: Built for **the commute**
slides.body: On weekdays, nearly half of all rides happen between 7 and 9 a.m. or 5 and 7 p.m. Last stretch from the subway to the office.

slides.headline: Riders **move the bikes**
slides.body: At rush hour some stations empty out and others overflow. Take a bike from a full one or return it to an empty one, and you earn points.

slides.headline: rides **in one year**
slides.body: That was 2024. In 2015, its first full year running, it was 113,000. More than 5 million people have signed up.

slides.headline: It **loses money**
slides.body: Ttareungyi lost about ₩12.7 billion in 2024. Seoul says that's fine: it's a public service, like a bus route, not a business.

slides.headline: Korea, explained **by a Korean.**
slides.body: Follow for the context behind the things Korea does.

caption:
In Seoul, a public bike costs ₩1,000 an hour. Grab one at a station, ride, and leave it at any other station.

More than 5 million people have signed up. It loses money every year, and Seoul keeps it anyway.

Would you ride one to work?
reply: New since last November: a 3-hour pass for ₩3,000, so you don't have to return the bike every 2 hours. Good for a long ride along the Han River. Does your city have public bikes?
fact_check: 2장: 2010년 440대 시범, 2015-10 정식 운영 — 서울시 보도자료(news.seoul.go.kr 515711). 이름 '따릉'은 자전거 벨 소리.
4장: 아무 대여소 반납, 앱 영어 버전 — 서울시 이용 안내.
5장: 365일 1시간권 30,000원, 요금 10년 동결 — 서울시 요금표(2026-03-10 수정), 서울시 적자 해명.
7장: 출퇴근 시간대 과다·과소 대여소 대여·반납 시 100마일리지 — 서울시.
9장: 적자 2023년 109억, 2024년 127억 — 서울시의회 이경숙 의원·서울시설공단 자료(더팩트 2025-09-06). 서울시 '교통복지 공공서비스' 입장.
제외: 2026-01 회원정보 450만 건 유출(2024 공격, 7월 30일권 보상) — 부정 이슈라 뺌.
